content.description: Job Introduction The Role As Tax Manager, you will be responsible for leading and overseeing all tax matters across the Superdry Group. Reporting into senior finance leadership, you will ensure that the Group meets its tax compliance and reporting obligations across all jurisdictions in which we operate. You will manage the relationship with external tax advisors who prepare and submit VAT returns globally, ensuring accuracy, timeliness and strong governance. You will take ownership of the Group’s overall tax framework, ensuring appropriate controls, policies and processes are in place. With one direct report focused on corporation tax, you will provide leadership, oversight and development support, while retaining accountability for all taxes (excluding payroll taxes and customs duty). This is a broad, hands-on role requiring strong technical expertise, commercial awareness and the ability to build effective relationships across the business. We're open to candidates across a range of experience levels for this position and would consider either a permanent or interim appointment, depending on the right fit for the business and the individual. You Will Own and manage the Group’s tax compliance framework across all territories in which we operate. Oversee the preparation and submission of all VAT returns globally through our external advisors, acting as the primary relationship lead. Manage and develop one direct report with responsibility for corporation tax compliance and reporting. Ensure accurate and timely corporation tax reporting, including review of tax provisions and disclosures for statutory and Group reporting. Act as the main point of contact for HMRC and overseas tax authorities, building and maintaining effective relationships. Manage relationships with external tax advisors, ensuring high-quality advice and value for money. Identify, assess and mitigate tax risks across the Group, implementing appropriate controls and policies. Support the management of the Group’s transfer pricing policies and documentation requirements. Provide clear, practical tax advice to key stakeholders across Finance and the wider business. Support finance transformation and process improvement initiatives to enhance tax governance and efficiency. You Are A qualified tax professional (CTA or equivalent) with post-qualification experience with broad exposure across corporate tax, VAT and international tax matters. Experienced in managing relationships with external advisors and tax authorities. Experience in managing and developing direct reports. Technically strong, with the ability to interpret complex legislation and translate it into practical business guidance. Commercially aware, understanding the impact of tax on business decisions. Highly organised, detail-oriented and able to manage competing priorities effectively. A strong communicator who can build effective relationships across functions and seniority levels. job_details.title: HR & Payroll Assistant - Brussels (Covering Belgium, France & Netherlands)

content.description:
The Role

Based in our Brussels office, reporting to our HR Manager Benelux, this role is responsible for providing HR administrative assistance and maintaining personnel data for our employees across Belgium and The Netherlands. This is a heavily administrative role that requires someone who is highly organised, a great communicator and who has previous HR & Payroll experience.

You will liaise with our stores, Store Managers and Area Managers to ensure the employee data for each of our stores and head office is accurate, in compliance with legal regulations and delivered in time for processing. You will deliver first line support for all HR & Payroll queries across the spectrum of the employee’s lifecycle from new hires to employees leaving the business.

Please be aware, that this role is for a minimum of 21 hours per week, but would consider candidates looking for more hours within the role.

You Will

Assist with obtaining proper backup and preparation of critical HR records and employee files, maintaining accuracy and legal compliance of all employee filesPrepare and process payroll information for all staff in Belgium, France and Netherlands in a timely and accurate manner, in conjunction with country Payroll Bureaus. This includes status changes, in-out service, hours worked and absences, social documents and fringe benefits. Liaise directly with all relevant Payroll Bureaus and be the point of contact for any queries from governmental institutions and other third parties regarding social documents. Carry out administration for HR processes - e.g. in and out of service, absence management, performance evaluations, contract management in line with internal and legal requirements. Act as the first point of contact and support for employees and managers for addressing and resolving day-to-day HR issues, coordinating with the HR Manager on any complicated issues. Assist with the development of internal processes and procedures and provide input to ensure optimal HR service to the organisation. Support the HR Manager with ad-hoc requests and projects. 

You Are

Experienced in HR and operational Payroll. Someone with a high level of attention to detail and excellent numeracy skills. Fluent in French and Dutch (spoken & written); good knowledge of English.Knowledgeable of Belgian labour laws and social regulations, and similar experience in Netherlands & France is highly desirable.Ideally educated to degree level in HR or equivalent working experience.Able to manage confidential and sensitive employee information in accordance with guidelines.Able to identify and escalate compliance issues where appropriate.Good at balancing multiple projects and day-to-day tasks, prioritising your workload successfully. Someone with excellent communication skills, able to build strong relationships and influence at all levels.
